Why We All Need to Make the Internet Fun Again

I can't help but notice the irony in this article being published by Recode, the company that got swallowed by AOL just a couple of weeks ago (contributing to the overall neutering of the internet by corporations).
Still, its a good article. I can see the homogenization of the web happening, but I'm more of a 'on the fringes' kind of guy. Actually, I think we all are, which is why we are on Voat, not reddit.

Hah yeah that's true, and it is a good read. I think it's also an an issue of critical mass, as the web's userbase gets bigger than ever before certain normative trends emerge. It just means that originality isn't as loud as it was before, but it's definitely still around.

Speaking of Reddit, this same article was posted there as well. I don't mean to sound condescending just because it's, well, Reddit, but half of the posts there sound like they were written more out of some knee jerk reaction then by people who actually gave the article some thought.

https://archive.is/7cBdJ

If you aren't finding the internet fun, you aren't going to the right places.

But seriously, I think the author is lamenting the standard evolution of a process. We see it everything: airplane design, manufacturing, even life itself. At first, everything is new and untested so any random design can be thrown out there. As time goes by the better (in the case of the internet read: popular) processes carve the design down. As time goes, the system is honed and refined so only a few designs are utilized. These designs are good enough to survive but may not be the best as the pressure for further adaption is not necessary (at the moment).

Their nothing stopping a free-spirited person from writing their own code to create their own social media (outside trademarks, copyrights, and patients that must be avoided). The problem is people already know how to use the tools that exist now. Assuming you don't make one that is worst or the same different, you need to convince people to learn all over again. Inertia is a hell of thing. Your tool has to be so much better that people have to go, 'had did we operate without it before' to get traction. A few better features isn't enough to learning a whole new thing.

Hello, and welcome to Tinfoilsec! I know you are probably eager to post, but if you want to be the most secure in posting here you should probably follow this list.

1. Are you new to voat? Do you still have to fill out captcha to post? If so, if you really want to be secure, you should wait until you no longer have to send captcha to google. Don't post anything you wouldn't want google to know. This board may be anonymized, but site admins and attackers can still see who we are, and so can google with their google analytics script and potentially with the captcha. We'll cover blocking analytics in the next step.

2. Are you on a phone? If so, that's not a great idea. especially if it's a smartphone. People in the right position can tell where you are based on what tower you are connected to, or where your phone's GPS says you are. Since your phone has closed source software and hardware, it's hard to tell if your phone is listening to you and doing who knows what. If thats bad enough, some police forces have set up these things called stingray towers which act as fake cellphone towers, which grab your personal data for them to examine. Welcome to a brave new world. Not so uncomfortable? As long as it's got something to connect to, many modern phones are designed to be able to determine your location and listen in to you as long as the hard to remove battery is still in them. It's best to leave your phone to your normal everyday activities, and keep it out of listening distance when you are at home.

3. How secure is your browser? Even on a more secure OS, an insecure browser can make all of that security half useless. If you are using Internet Explorer or Chrome/Chromium, you are making a big mistake. If Chrome being there surprises you, take a look at this: https://8ch.net/tech/chrome.html As the page suggests, you should try out GNU Icecat, or at least Firefox, and have at the bare minimum these addons: 1. Noscript (when using this, only enable scripts when you absolutely must. Make sure you keep google analytics blocked on vote) 2. HTTPS Everywhere (if your really paranoid, also get HTTP nowhere and try using ixquick proxy to go to the sites that vb) 3. Self Destructing Cookies (only enable cookies to stay forever if you truly trust these sites)

4. How secure is your internet? If you aren't using 1 or 2 VPN's at once you should look into them. At least check out OpenNIC and how to use DNScrypt. Don't bother trying to access this subverse with TOR or I2P, because the former is insecure and the latter is way too slow.

5. How secure is your computer as a whole? If you are using Windows and Mac there is a good chance you are being tracked, especially with possible malware being on your computer. Even with GNU/Linux (aka what Linux on most PC's is properly called) you run the risk of being insecure because you may or may not have proprietary software (like skype, steam, possibly your graphics card driver, your terrible broadcom wireless driver, etc) installed. If you want to be secure in some ways without making much compromise, your best off getting a seperate computer to do secure things on. Get a used Thinkpad that's capable of having it's bios flashed with libreboot http://www.libreboot.org/docs/hcl/index.html#supported_list and install Trisquel GNU/Linux on it (it's fully open source). if your paranoid because Trisquel uses Ubuntu binaries, there are other good alternatives like Debian, Parabola, and maybe Qubes OS. Keep in mind that you still have security vulnerabilities despite this, as programmers aren't perfect and some are probably paid by the NSA, other government agencies across the globe, and corporations to write in hard to find security holes in GNU/Linux. But at least people can find these vulnerabilities, unlike in proprietary software.

I will add more info to this later. See anything that is wrong, then feel free to correct me,
Before you post here, you might want to do these things.
